query: You are the lead database engineer for StreamForge, a media streaming startup that uses Cloud Bigtable for real time session telemetry. The business requires very high durability and an objective to restore service in under 10 minutes if data is deleted or becomes corrupted. Which approach should you implement to meet these goals?

options.text: Schedule daily Cloud Bigtable exports to Cloud Storage and restore with the Bigtable import tool when needed
options.explanation: This approach relies on periodic full exports to object storage and uses the native import utility for table restoration.

options.text: Enable Cloud Bigtable replication with two or more clusters in different zones and direct traffic to a hot standby cluster during recovery
options.explanation: This approach establishes multi cluster replication so applications can quickly fail over to a prewarmed cluster if the primary is impaired.

options.text: Periodically copy Cloud Bigtable data into Cloud SQL and use the Cloud SQL copy as the recovery source
options.explanation: This approach moves NoSQL data into a relational service to maintain a separate copy for restoration.

options.text: Use Dataflow with Cloud Bigtable change streams to continuously write mutations to Cloud Storage and recover by replaying files
options.explanation: This approach streams row level changes to files in object storage that can be replayed to rebuild a dataset.

answer:
The correct option is Enable Cloud Bigtable replication with two or more clusters in different zones and direct traffic to a hot standby cluster during recovery.

Bigtable replication stores your tables in multiple clusters across zones which increases durability because there are independent copies of the data. During an outage you can meet a ten minute recovery time objective by routing traffic to the standby cluster using multi cluster routing or by updating your clients to target the healthy cluster. This approach restores service quickly because there is no bulk data movement during failover.

Schedule daily Cloud Bigtable exports to Cloud Storage and restore with the Bigtable import tool when needed is too slow for a ten minute objective. Exports introduce a recovery point of up to a day and imports of large tables take far longer than a few minutes.

Periodically copy Cloud Bigtable data into Cloud SQL and use the Cloud SQL copy as the recovery source is a poor fit because Cloud SQL is a relational service and does not match Bigtable scale or access patterns. The copy process and any cutover would exceed a ten minute objective.

Use Dataflow with Cloud Bigtable change streams to continuously write mutations to Cloud Storage and recover by replaying files adds durability outside Bigtable but replaying mutations from files at scale is complex and usually cannot restore service within ten minutes.

tip: When you see a very tight recovery time objective look for native replication that allows quick traffic rerouting. Export and replay based strategies usually miss an under ten minutes target at real Bigtable scales.

query: A subscription platform at scrumtuous.com operates a regional Cloud SQL for MySQL deployment with a primary instance and a failover instance in different zones. The team created three read replicas to offload reporting queries and now wants to evenly spread read-only traffic across the replicas while providing connection pooling from the application layer with minimal code changes. Which approach should they take?

options.text: Configure an Internal TCP Proxy Load Balancer in front of the MySQL read replicas to distribute client connections
options.explanation: An Internal TCP Proxy Load Balancer accepts TCP traffic and forwards connections to regional backend targets.

options.text: Build a Cloud Dataflow pipeline that fans out read queries across all read replicas
options.explanation: Cloud Dataflow runs batch and streaming data processing jobs that can connect to various data sources.

options.text: Run ProxySQL between the application and Cloud SQL so it performs read write split and pools and balances read connections across replicas
options.explanation: ProxySQL is a MySQL aware proxy that can route queries with rules and maintain efficient connection pools for backend instances.

options.text: Use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy on each application server to multiplex and load balance connections to all read replicas
options.explanation: The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy secures and manages database connections and integrates with IAM for a specified Cloud SQL instance.

answer:
The correct option is Run ProxySQL between the application and Cloud SQL so it performs read write split and pools and balances read connections across replicas. Using ProxySQL lets the app continue speaking the MySQL protocol to a single endpoint while the proxy handles connection pooling and read distribution to the replicas and routes writes to the primary with minimal code change.

ProxySQL is MySQL aware so it can perform read write splitting based on query type and send read queries to a reader host group that includes all read replicas. It supports connection pooling and multiplexing which reduces connection overhead to Cloud SQL. It can also monitor replication lag and avoid sending traffic to stale replicas which keeps reporting traffic both balanced and safe.

Configure an Internal TCP Proxy Load Balancer in front of the MySQL read replicas to distribute client connections is incorrect because Cloud SQL instances are not supported load balancer backends and the TCP proxy is not query aware. It cannot perform read write split or database connection pooling.

Build a Cloud Dataflow pipeline that fans out read queries across all read replicas is incorrect because Dataflow is for batch and streaming data processing rather than interactive SQL query routing. It would require substantial application changes and provides no native MySQL connection pooling or read write splitting.

Use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy on each application server to multiplex and load balance connections to all read replicas is incorrect because the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy is for secure authentication and connectivity to a specific instance. It does not load balance across multiple instances and it does not perform read write split or provide the type of pooling and replica balancing needed here.
